chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 450: Twin Lotus Horror & Bai Lingmiao’s Growing Resolve
chapter_meta_description: Bai Lingmiao dismisses Lü Xiucai’s cowardice, questions Li Huowang’s sanity, and burns forbidden texts. But a twisted presence hides within the White Lotus mural—unseen.
og_title: “A Madman Getting Stronger Isn’t Good News.” — Bai Lingmiao’s Hard Truths in Ch. 450
og_description: Bai Lingmiao refuses to trust Li Huowang’s reassurances. Chun Xiaoman cheerfully suggests burning a cult’s human-sacrifice manuals. And the mural that shouldn’t exist starts to … move.
twitter_title: Chapter 450: The scary thing isn’t the monster—it’s Bai Lingmiao losing faith in Li Huowang’s “I’m fine.”
twitter_description: A quiet, ominous chapter where books burn, cowardice is mocked, and a twin lotus harbors something inside-out.

lore_anchors.definition: A traditional Chinese symbol of two lotuses growing from a single stem, representing inseparable love or marital unity. In this novel, it appears after haunting chanting and hides a disturbing, inverted presence.
A key deity in Chinese folk sectarian traditions (often linked to White Lotus and Luo teachings). She is the creator-mother who calls her children back to the “Native Land of True Emptiness.”
A form of spirit possession that grants the medium superhuman combat abilities, strength, and resistance to pain, distinct from passive divination possession.
A traditional Chinese saying expressing a wife’s resigned loyalty to her husband’s fate. Bai Lingmiao uses it to affirm her commitment to Li Huowang despite his insanity.
